references.text: The Lord's command to Joshua to lame the horses and burn the chariots – this is the direct order that Joshua obeys in verse 9
The Mosaic law forbids the king from acquiring many horses, showing God's will that Israel should not rely on military power
Some trust in chariots and some in horses, but we call upon the name of the Lord – illustrating the principle behind destroying the enemy's military equipment
David lamed the horses of Hadadezer, king of Zobah, in the same way that Joshua did here
Woe to those who go down to Egypt for help and rely on horses – warning against trusting in military power rather than the Lord
Not by might nor by power, but by my Spirit, says the Lord – the principle of not relying on human military strength
